Architecture

Commitment Pool MVP (Tibi's experiment)

The architecture of Tibi's commitment-pool-experiment branch at 00f6c0d, drawn as it stands: a Group is a pool, a Commitment lives on its NDO, and fulfillment is one closure that writes the event, the claim and two verifiable receipts. Every box marked new or modified is what the branch adds over dev at c18e926 (the merge of #183); unmarked boxes are already on dev. Companion of the review notes on the branch, which hold the line-level findings.

How to work it: walk the maps (double-click a box to open its level), open a box for its spec, then pick on each decision card. The decisions are only the ones that concern dev; the experiment's own calls are Tibi's, listed under Evidence, and the open points on the pool's authorisation are findings on the PR board.

Decisions

Pick one option per decision; my lean is starred. Nothing below is decided until you pick, and your picks and notes leave with copy my answers or Send.

D1 How does dev take the design-system package? decided

Soushi wants the design-system adapters (ndo-ui-adapters.ts, governance-template-map.ts) on dev. They import @nondominium/ndo-ui, which the branch takes as file:../../nondominium-design-system/packages/ndo-ui plus Vite aliases. A fresh clone and CI cannot resolve that path.

My lean, Publish @nondominium/ndo-ui to npm with a version: The adapters are the boundary between design-system and DHT types; they only make sense on dev with a dependency every machine resolves.

Consequences: Soushi, 2026-11-13: the design system stays private, so no npm publish; it comes in as a nix flake input (decision recorded in #205, v0.3). The file: path and the Vite aliases go.

touches Nondominium design system, Design-system shell, Design-system adapters

D2 Which slice of the experiment reaches dev next? decided

#183 took the protocol-general backend. What remains: the Use and Consume fork on NDO identity (five Sweettests), the pool (Tibi's experiment), the design-system UI remix.

My lean, The Use and Consume fork, now: Same reasoning that sent the backend through #183: it is not pool-specific and it carries its tests.

Consequences: Soushi, 2026-11-13, against my lean: the design-system adapters come next (#205), then the Use and Consume fork (#204); both sit in v0.3. The pool stays on the branch.

touches NDO identity, Shared types, Design-system shell

D3 Should initial_quantity reach dev as a Measure? decided

Only if D2 brings the fork to dev. The branch adds initial_quantity as Option<f64> beside default_unit: Option<String>, after #183 moved every other quantity to Measure.

My lean, Port it as Option<Measure>: A new integrity field costs nothing to shape now and a DNA change later.

Consequences: #204 lands initial_quantity as Option<Measure>.

touches NDO identity, Shared types

D4 Capability slots in v0.2 decided

Soushi, 2026-11-13: plan the capability slot for the v0.2 milestone. The CS substrate (REQ-NDO-CS-01 to 04, 06) is not coded; #99 and #156 wait on it, and Tibi's section 8.3 names a CustomApp(CommitmentPool) slot as its NDO-side index. Filed as #184.

My lean, Substrate only in v0.2, slot types as their own issues: Three consumers already wait on the substrate; it should not wait on any one of them.

Consequences: #184 is the substrate in v0.2, on Soushi's lane with hREA (#185); file-storage (#99) follows in v0.2, Flowsta (#156) and the pool slot later.

touches NDO identity, Commitment anchor

D5 What comes first, capability slots or work contexts? decided

Asked on this board at 16:27. Work contexts live in the group DHT (ADR of #168); capability slots attach to the NDO identity. Nothing filed makes one depend on the other.

My lean, Capability slots in v0.2, work contexts in v0.3: Two open issues already wait on the slot substrate; work contexts have no waiting consumer yet.

Consequences: Soushi, 2026-11-13 16:13 and 16:32: slots (#184) in v0.2, work contexts (#201) in v0.3. v0.2 lanes: Soushi on hREA and slots, Tibi on NDO Layer 1 (#206, #207, #141, #144), plus the standalone release (#203).

touches NDO identity, Commitment anchor

ifadmit function rust
pub struct AdmitCommitmentInput {

  pub ndo_dna_hash: DnaHash,
  pub network_seed: String,

#[hdk_extern] pub fn get_pool_contents(group_hash: ActionHash) -> ExternResult<Vec<PoolEntry>>
Contract:

Admit writes an anchor in status Admitted and links it from the group. Withdraw supersedes the latest version with status Withdrawn and refuses a stale previous hash. The pool read returns both statuses.

iffulfill function rust
pub struct FulfillCommitmentClosureInput {
  pub commitment_hash: ActionHash,
  pub observed_quantity: Measure,
  pub resource_state_update: Option<OperationalState>,
  pub provider_metrics: PerformanceMetrics,
  pub receiver_metrics: PerformanceMetrics,
  pub note: Option<String>,
}
#[hdk_extern] pub fn fulfill_commitment_closure(input: FulfillCommitmentClosureInput)
  -> ExternResult<FulfillCommitmentClosureOutput>
Contract:

Called by the party who did not author the commitment. The author's conductor countersigns a payload it rebuilds itself; a fulfilled commitment is refused on both sides. A resource state update needs the caller to be its custodian.

ifmode type rust
pub enum EconomicMode { Use, Consume }
pub enum UseKind { Unit, Capacity }
pub enum ClosureReason { Depleted, Spoiled, Withdrawn, WrittenOff, DonatedRemainder, Other }
Contract:

Set on NondominiumIdentity at creation and immutable after. Use needs a UseKind, Capacity needs max_concurrent_users of 2 or more, Consume needs a unit, a positive initial quantity and an identification pattern. A Consume NDO closes with a reason.

Evidence

Source of this board: the branch's own summary documentation/Applications/commitment-pool-experiment.md (sections 5 to 8), checked against the code at 00f6c0d.

Tibi's locked decisions, as his doc states them:

QuestionHis choice
What is a pool?A Group cell
Where does the commitment live?On the NDO cell; the pool only points
Who may admit?Any group member (not enforced in validation; see the PR board)
WithdrawalA status mark, never a delete (pool memory)
Fulfillmentcall_remote countersign inside one closure; offline counterparty fails cleanly
Pool listingGroup-side CommitmentAnchor, not a CapabilitySlot (CS is not coded yet)
Inventoriable forkUse or Consume on Layer 0, Physical and Hybrid only
Consume identityThe NDO is the batch; a new delivery is a new NDO
Batch closureEndOfLife or Deprecated with a closure_reason such as Depleted
Design systemSibling checkout of release-prototype through a Vite alias
Merge to devNot automatic; slices after Grassroots Economics feedback
